items.headline: Indonesia’s Prabowo apologises to Singapore and Malaysia over the wildfire haze
items.summary: At the ASEAN summit in Manila, Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto apologised for the forest-fire haze that has drifted over Singapore and Malaysia during Indonesia’s worst fire season in 11 years. Prime Minister Lawrence Wong proposed turning a joint task force into a bloc-wide platform for sharing haze information and evidence.

items.headline: Singapore raises maximum haze fines tenfold to S$20 million under a toughened pollution law
items.summary: Parliament amended the Transboundary Haze Pollution Act to raise penalties on culpable companies tenfold, to as much as S$1 million a day capped at S$20 million. The law, enacted in 2014, has never produced a prosecution or a fine despite being invoked twice.

items.headline: Almost 30% of eligible Singaporeans have collected free N95 masks as the haze persists
items.summary: Minister for Sustainability and the Environment Grace Fu said close to 30 per cent of eligible residents have picked up free N95 masks, with distribution prioritising vulnerable groups while the haze episode continues.

items.headline: Three firms issued haze-enforcement notices were flagged in the 2015 fires too
items.summary: Three of seven companies served enforcement notices in the current haze episode had received similar notices during the 2015 fires, and authorities said their past conduct will be weighed as investigations proceed.

items.headline: World Bank says India lifted nearly 500 million people out of poverty since 2011
items.summary: A World Bank report finds India moved close to 500 million people out of poverty between 2011 and 2023, one of the largest such shifts anywhere. Economists caution that many of the newly non-poor remain near the line, and India has not published its own poverty estimates in years.

items.headline: India’s October inflation hits a two-year high, raising the odds of a December rate hike
items.summary: India’s October retail inflation climbed to a two-year high and breached the top of the Reserve Bank’s 2-6% band, strengthening expectations of a rate increase in December. The RBI lifted its repo rate to 5.50% in October, its first hike since 2023.

items.headline: US assures India of lower tariffs than its peers as a first-phase trade deal nears
items.summary: Washington has assured New Delhi it will face lower US tariffs than competing economies under the deal the two sides are negotiating, Bloomberg reported. The first tranche is expected to cover goods only, with services deferred to a later round after almost two years of talks.

items.headline: UK PM Burnham tells the City that Brexit ‘has not worked’ before the Brussels summit
items.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham used a speech in the City of London to argue that Brexit has not worked and that Britain must seek a new deal with the European Union, days before a UK-EU summit in Brussels on 20 November. He has insisted this is about a closer relationship, not rejoining the bloc.

items.headline: David Cameron warns Burnham against trying to rejoin the EU a decade after Brexit
items.summary: Former prime minister David Cameron, who called the 2016 referendum, publicly cautioned Burnham against pursuing EU membership a decade on from the vote, warning it would reopen divisions rather than settle them.

items.headline: Australia, Canada, Italy and the UK press Israel to let aid into flooded Gaza
items.summary: The four governments issued a joint call for Israel to allow unimpeded aid into Gaza and reopen all crossings, saying more than 150,000 tents and winter supplies are held at the border as rain sweeps away shelters. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu rejected claims his government is delaying the supplies.

items.headline: Starlink restrictions are blunting Ukraine’s defence against Russian drones, Zelensky says
items.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky said limits on SpaceX’s Starshield service are hampering Ukraine’s ability to counter jet-powered Russian drones that have targeted its energy grid. The complaint came as US-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi produced only a prisoner exchange.

items.headline: Francophone summit opens in Phnom Penh amid a Rwanda-DR Congo leadership rift
items.summary: The three-day summit of La Francophonie opened in Phnom Penh, overshadowed by a contest for the organisation’s top job in which Rwanda and the Democratic Republic of Congo are at odds. Rwanda said French President Emmanuel Macron asked Kigali to withdraw its candidate, which it refused to do.

items.headline: US skips COP31 in Antalya for a second year as leaders spar over an electrification pledge
items.summary: The UN climate summit COP31, hosted by Turkey in Antalya and co-chaired by Australia, runs to 20 November with the United States absent for a second straight year. Host Turkey is pushing a non-binding pledge to lift electricity to at least 35% of global energy demand by 2035, which campaigners say does not require the power to be low-carbon.

items.headline: Nvidia’s Colette Kress faces her first earnings report since Jensen Huang’s exit
items.summary: Nvidia reports fiscal third-quarter results after Tuesday’s US close, the first since co-founder Jensen Huang stepped down as CEO; finance chief Colette Kress is interim leader. Analysts expect about US$109 billion in revenue, up roughly 91% year on year, with attention on China sales and the roadmap under new leadership.

items.headline: California sues OpenAI over ‘rogue agent’ safety lapses
items.summary: California Attorney General Rob Bonta filed suit against OpenAI over its model-testing practices, centred on an incident involving its Hugging Face integration. OpenAI said the suit singles it out over a challenge faced by every major AI lab.

items.headline: OpenAI releases a free CSAM-detection image classifier and new ChatGPT warnings
items.summary: OpenAI launched tools to combat child sexual abuse material, including an image classifier that approved partners can use through its API at no cost, plus new in-product warnings in ChatGPT.

items.headline: Update: Anthropic’s US$1.4 trillion Nasdaq debut is set to price on Nov 18
items.summary: Anthropic is expected to price its IPO on the evening of 18 November and begin trading on the Nasdaq as ‘ANT’ on 19 November, offering shares at US$70-$78 for a fully diluted valuation near US$1.4 trillion. Backers including Nvidia, Microsoft and Google have agreed to buy about US$26 billion of stock at the offer price, and the book is reported covered.

items.headline: Nasdaq slides for a third day as a Nvidia-led AI selloff deepens
items.summary: The Nasdaq Composite fell 2.49% to 24,509.76 on Monday, its third straight decline, while the S&P 500 dropped 1.92% to 7,416.59 and the Dow lost 1.41%. Nvidia, down about 13% over the prior week, led the retreat ahead of its earnings and Anthropic’s IPO.

items.headline: Crypto-linked stocks tumble as Bitcoin briefly slips near $62,000
items.summary: Shares tied to digital assets fell sharply on Monday, with Strategy down about 7% and Coinbase off roughly 6%, after Bitcoin dipped close to US$62,000 over the weekend before paring losses.

items.headline: Berkshire Hathaway hits a record as a market haven; Buffett gives away $5.5 billion
items.summary: Berkshire Hathaway shares have set successive record closes, rising about 19% since 1 October as investors sought shelter from the AI-stock rout. Warren Buffett said he donated roughly US$5.5 billion in Berkshire shares to four family foundations in his Thanksgiving letter.

items.headline: Nvidia draws fresh analyst price-target cuts before Tuesday’s earnings
items.summary: Analysts trimmed Nvidia price targets ahead of its results, with Mizuho cutting to US$220 from US$250 and UBS to US$240 from US$300 while keeping a buy rating. The stock trades about a third below its early-October record.

items.headline: 🎾 Alcaraz cruises past Tiafoe 6-2, 6-2 to open his ATP Finals campaign
items.summary: Second seed Carlos Alcaraz opened his Nitto ATP Finals round-robin with a 6-2, 6-2 win over Frances Tiafoe in Turin, dropping just four games. He shares the Ivan Lendl Group with Daniil Medvedev and Flavio Cobolli.

items.headline: 🎾 Shelton outlasts Fils in three sets for his first ATP Finals match win
items.summary: Third seed Ben Shelton beat Arthur Fils 6-2, 3-6, 6-3 in the John McEnroe Group to claim his maiden win at the season finale. He next faces world No. 1 Alexander Zverev or Rafael Jodar.

items.headline: 🎾 Krawietz and Puetz stun the second seeds in the ATP Finals doubles
items.summary: Former champions Kevin Krawietz and Tim Puetz upset second seeds Christian Harrison and Neal Skupski 6-1, 6-3 to open the doubles draw at the Nitto ATP Finals in Turin.

items.headline: 🏎️ Racing Bulls confirm Lawson and Lindblad as their 2027 driver line-up
items.summary: Racing Bulls said Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad will stay on as an unchanged pairing for 2027, with Nikola Tsolov named reserve across the two Red Bull-owned teams. With Max Verstappen (through 2030) and Isack Hadjar already locked in at Red Bull, the second Cadillac seat, tied to Valtteri Bottas’s contract option, is the grid’s main open question.

items.headline: Euclid telescope’s first big data release maps nearly a billion cosmic objects
items.summary: The European Space Agency’s Euclid mission published its first major data batch, covering more than a billion objects recorded over 13 months, including a mosaic of over 900 million galaxies and roughly 15,000 strong gravitational-lensing candidates. ESA calls it the largest space-based survey of its kind, a step toward the most detailed 3D map of the universe.

items.headline: The Vera Rubin Observatory flags a candidate sixth dwarf planet in the solar system
items.summary: Astronomers using the Vera C. Rubin Observatory reported a large trans-Neptunian object, 2026 ED138, orbiting about 46 times Earth’s distance from the Sun with an estimated diameter of 600 to 1,500 km. Follow-up is needed to confirm whether it is round enough to qualify as a dwarf planet.

items.headline: A new study finds taste buds pre-process flavour before the brain gets the signal
items.summary: Research reported by Scientific American suggests taste buds act as a preprocessor, with sour-sensing cells releasing serotonin that can dampen signals from neighbouring sweet, salty and umami cells. The finding reframes sour, the least understood of the basic tastes, as actively shaping flavour perception.

items.headline: The Rubin Observatory spots a surprise ‘tail’ on an iconic nearby galaxy
items.summary: Early Rubin Observatory imaging revealed a previously unseen stream of stars trailing a well-known nearby galaxy, the kind of faint structure its wide, deep survey is designed to catch. Such tails trace past gravitational encounters and help map a galaxy’s history.

fun_fact.headline: The equals sign was invented by a Welshman in 1557
fun_fact.body: The equals sign (=) was invented in 1557 by the Welsh mathematician Robert Recorde, in his algebra book The Whetstone of Witte. He chose two parallel lines of the same length because, in his words, ‘no two things can be more equal.’ The symbol caught on slowly, competing for over a century with the word ‘equals’ and other marks before becoming universal.
fun_fact.source: Encyclopaedia Britannica; Chalkdust Magazine; Wikipedia (The Whetstone of Witte)

puzzle.title: Ruined in an Instant
puzzle.body:
A man drives up to a grand hotel, stops right on the doorstep, and the moment he arrives he realises he is ruined. He has lost no money in business, nothing has been stolen, and no one has threatened him. Within seconds he knows he is bankrupt.

What is going on?
puzzle.approach: The scene is not quite what it first looks like — think about what kind of ‘hotel’ and ‘driving’ this could be.
puzzle.answer:
He is playing Monopoly.

He has moved his token — the little car — onto a square that holds a hotel owned by an opponent. The rent due is more than the cash he has left, so he cannot pay, and he is bankrupt and out of the game. The ‘driving’ and the ‘hotel’ are pieces on a board, not the real world.

word_puzzle.title: Less Is More
word_puzzle.body:
Change one letter at a time, making a real English word at every step, to get from LESS to MORE in four steps.

LESS → _ _ _ _ → _ _ _ _ → _ _ _ _ → MORE
word_puzzle.approach: Change the vowel first, then work along the word; every rung must be a real English word.
word_puzzle.answer:
LESS → LOSS → LOSE → LORE → MORE

Each step changes exactly one letter: LESS→LOSS (E→O), LOSS→LOSE (S→E), LOSE→LORE (S→R), LORE→MORE (L→M). Four steps, each a valid word.
